verdict.rationale: LiveKit Agents runs as plain Python/Node.js programs that join rooms as programmatic participants, with no UI involved. Its behavioral tests plug into pytest or Vitest suites, and agent simulations run end-to-end conversations. Hands-on probes show the CLI, a dev-mode server and the pip package all running with no account or key, which suits unattended automation, but CI pipeline usage is only implied, not explicitly documented. Missing for 10: explicit first-party docs on running agents or tests in CI pipelines (e.g. GitHub Actions examples, CI flags or env configuration), documented non-interactive/headless CLI automation workflows, independent corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The Agents framework lets you add any Python or Node.js program to LiveKit rooms as full realtime participants.
They integrate with your existing test suite using pytest (Python) or Vitest (Node.js)
Agent simulations run end-to-end conversations between your agent and an LLM-driven user, then evaluate the results across the full interaction.
`livekit-server --dev` (brew-installed, Apache-2.0 OSS) booted on this machine with NO account or key
`lk --version` printed `lk version 2.18.6` after a plain `brew install livekit-cli` — the official CLI runs keylessly.
